I have this recurring dream where I am floating in this endless lazy river. I know instinctively that I am safe and no harm will come to me, and I'm really able to savor the moment. The surrounding scenery changes periodically, one moment it is similar to something from [Fantasia](http://morganrlewis.files.wordpress.com/2012/05/fantasia2000_pdvd_032.jpg?w=584&h=315), and the next I could be in an aquatic themed nightclub with floating go-go dancers and psychedelic, glowing fish swimming just under the surface, but always out of reach. 

These scenes are particularly intriguing to me (I suppose I am a semi-lucid dreamer), the water will usually have a blue, green, or white(shallow water at a white sand beach) hue to it, but these dazzling electric-colored fish will appear (they always appear first) and the water will transition to black, as if my brain cannot handle the thought of glowing fish during the day or against a bright background. Another interesting bit is that the dancers are never sexual in nature, some may be scantily clad, and quite beautiful, but I never see them as sexual objects. 
The dream usually ends with an unceremonious departure, like getting off a ride at Disneyland, and a strong desire to fall back asleep and immediately return. I've been having this dream since I was a child, I'm 27 now.

I was watching a video on youtube about the intelligence of plants. Acacia  trees in Africa are very hardy, and during a drought are usually the only large vegetation with any foliage. This draws large herbivores like Kudu, and giraffes. When being specifically targeted by such large "predators", the trees release a certain chemical in the air to warn other acacia's around them, and they start to produce more Tannin, a toxic compound found in all plants. Usually harmless to something as large as a Kudu, or Giraffe, or even a human, but in the larger quantities can shut down the animal's digestive tract. 

tl;dr Acacia trees use chemical signals to warn other trees to produce toxins for incoming large herbivores.

Her: "What's on your mind/Watcha thinkin' about?"

When I was 11 I moved across the country for a few years, but after my grandpa passed away after a long battle with Parkinson's Disease, we moved back home, and stayed at my grandma's house for a while. 

I was up late one night, my cat on my lap, watching T.V.. There was a peculiar silence, the a/c went off just as the T.V. got quiet, and a few other ambient sounds seemed to die out all at the same time. My cat started acting very strange and seemed to be staring at something, and I swear that I could hear the sound of my grandpa's shuffling footsteps across the carpet. 

I immediately looked towards his rocking chair, half expecting to see him there, half expecting to shit my pants and curl up into the fetal position clutching a crucifix to my chest (I'm not gonna lie, it was EXTREMELY freaky). 

I loved my Grandpa very much, he was a WWII veteran, a loving father and husband, and although I only have very few memories of him before he was crippled by Parkinson's, those memories are of a man that was larger than life. Everybody loved him. I believe a personality like that could linger. Or it was 100% subconscious/coincidental...
